issue_context.title: GDScript 2.0: Export group annotations show in documentation
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

v4.0.alpha.custom_build [d26442e70]

### System information

Arch on 5.18.10-arch1-1

### Issue description

Given code:

```gdscript
extends Node

@export_group("Hello")
@export var world: int

```

Open it in docs, and `Variant Hello` is shown
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/14253836/178505058-97c9ee4b-84a0-4960-85f2-932c22e171d2.png)


### Steps to reproduce

1) Use the code above

### Minimal reproduction project

[test9.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/9093545/test9.zip)

review_comments:
```suggestion
		if (props[i].usage & (PROPERTY_USAGE_CATEGORY | PROPERTY_USAGE_GROUP | PROPERTY_USAGE_SUBGROUP)) {
```

99% sure this will work the same, and is arguably more readable, but if anyone disagrees that's fine.
@nathanfranke It's not the same thing. Your way will only work if usage has all 3 flags set at once.
if the usages are `0b001`, `0b010`, and `0b100`, `x | y | z` will be `0b111` and `usage & (x | y | z)` will be truthy if any flag is enabled.

Let's merge as is, but this could be a relevant cleanup PR as it seems we use both styles currently:
```
$ rg "usage & \(PROPERTY_USAGE.*\| PROPERTY_USAGE.*\)" | wc -l
16

$ rg "usage & PROPERTY_USAGE.* \|\| .*usage & PROPERTY_USAGE.*" | wc -l
11
```
